We assessed cardiac synchrony as the cross-correlation of residualized inter-beat interval (IBI) time series from synchronized electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings. Results showed that greater mutual liking, gender match, and shared emotional perception were linked to stronger cardiac synchrony, suggesting that interpersonal synchrony reflects social and emotional alignment even between strangers. Additionally, the similarity between the heart rate variability (HRV) of each interaction partner predicted greater synchrony, indicating that physiological compatibility may facilitate alignment. We also examined whether a brief mindfulness induction given to the support provider enhanced synchrony and interaction quality. However, the mindfulness induction had no significant effect, suggesting that a brief self-regulation practice may not influence physiological alignment in first-time interactions. These findings extend research on interpersonal cardiac synchrony beyond established relationships, identifying key factors that shape physiological alignment during emotional sharing in first-time interactions.

title: Effects of External Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation on Neurocognitive Functioning in Children and Adolescents With ADHD: A Phase 2b Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with atypical cognition and related autonomic nervous system regulation. Trigeminal nerve stimulation (TNS) received U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance as neuromodulation treatment for ADHD based on findings of clinical improvements from a pilot trial that were not confirmed in the authors' larger multicenter UK trial. Effects of TNS on cognition in ADHD, however, are relatively unknown. The authors therefore tested secondary outcomes, that is, short- and longer-term effects of active versus sham TNS in youths with ADHD on a broad neurocognitive task battery, physiological indicators of autonomic nervous system regulation, and head motion. In the first confirmatory, multicenter, double-blind, parallel-group, phase 2b randomized sham-controlled trial, 150 youths with ADHD (ages 8-18 years) were assigned to 4 weeks of nightly active (N=75) or sham (N=75) TNS. Cognitive performance was assessed using a comprehensive battery of executive function and attention tasks (inhibition, sustained attention, time estimation, processing speed, and intrasubject response variability) at baseline, posttreatment, and 6-month follow-up. Autonomic nervous system regulation (heart rate, heart rate variability, and electrodermal activity) was measured via a wristband device and head motion with an eye tracker during rest or cognitive testing. Intention-to-treat analysis showed no significant differential treatment effects between active and sham TNS on any cognitive or physiological outcomes after 4 weeks of treatment or on cognitive measures at 6-month follow-up. TNS does not appear to improve neurocognitive performance, autonomic regulation, or head motion in youths with ADHD, extending negative clinical findings. The findings do not provide evidence to support TNS as a viable treatment to improve cognitive or autonomic nervous system functioning in youths with ADHD.

title: Transcriptomic Network Analysis Reveals Trauma Type- and Ancestry-Related Heterogeneity in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder.
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a debilitating psychiatric disorder that frequently co-occurs with major depressive disorder (MDD), a comorbidity that is partly attributable to shared genetic heritability and common environmental risk factors. Despite extensive efforts to identify peripheral transcriptomic biomarkers, findings have been inconsistent, potentially reflecting the substantial biological heterogeneity underlying these disorders. The primary goal of this study was to identify molecular signatures that reflect the clinical and biological heterogeneity of PTSD and MDD. The authors present a network analysis of blood-based transcriptomics from 466 pregnant women in South Africa, including 215 individuals with PTSD and/or MDD (mean age, 26.34 years [SD=5.77]) and 251 trauma-exposed control participants (mean age, 27.14 years [SD=5.82]). Gene expression modules associated with trauma-related phenotypes were identified, including childhood adversity, intimate partner violence, and recent life stress, as well as ancestry and depressive symptoms, highlighting multiple sources of molecular variation. To evaluate the predictive relevance of these transcriptomic features, random forest models were applied using a nested cross-validation framework with permutation testing. Models achieved moderate and statistically significant performance in predicting trauma-related phenotypes (mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], ~0.61-0.69 across models [SD=0.07-0.10]), whereas prediction of PTSD or MDD diagnosis showed near-chance performance (mean AUROC=0.52, SD=0.03). These findings suggest that peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures are more strongly associated with trauma exposure profiles and population background than with diagnostic status. Collectively, the results support exposure-informed stratification as a complementary framework to traditional diagnostic categories for capturing biologically meaningful heterogeneity.

title: Fast Multiparametric ASL MRI via Multi-Dimensional Acceleration and Subspace Reconstruction.
abstract: Multi-post-labeling delays (PLDs) multi-echo times (TEs) arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI enables simultaneous quantification of cerebral blood flow (CBF), arterial transit time (ATT), and blood-brain barrier (BBB) water exchange, but requires long scan times due to the combination of multi-TEs, PLDs, and repeated control-label acquisitions. A five-dimensional (5D) acquisition and reconstruction framework was developed to enable accelerated multi-parametric ASL. A coordinated undersampling strategy was designed across in-plane k-space, through-plane k-space, TE, and control-label measurement dimensions, achieving a combined acceleration factor of approximately 28. Reconstruction was performed using a Kronecker-structured subspace model that exploited low-rank correlations along the TE and control-label dimensions. Sparsity regularization was applied in the subspace coefficient domain, and temporal bases were estimated from a single fully sampled middle slice. The framework was evaluated using in vivo echo-time-resolved ASL (TASL) datasets from eight subjects. The proposed reconstruction outperformed a matched compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction across all echo times, yielding higher structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), with the largest improvements observed under severe undersampling (R≈28) and at late echo times. Higher-fidelity CBF, ATT, BBB, and intravascular transit time (ITT) maps were obtained, with the greatest gains observed for BBB and ITT. Test-retest reliability, assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), remained comparable to fully sampled reference data. Coordinated multi-dimensional undersampling combined with Kronecker subspace reconstruction enables highly accelerated multi-parametric ASL while preserving image quality, quantitative parameter estimation, and test-retest reliability, supporting clinically feasible acquisition times.

title: Neurodivergent Characteristics and Treatment Outcomes for Patients and Carers: A Secondary Analysis of the TRIANGLE Trial for Anorexia Nervosa.
journal: The International journal of eating disorders
abstract: Neurodivergent characteristics, such as autistic and obsessive-compulsive features, may be associated with poorer treatment outcomes in anorexia nervosa (AN). We used data from the TRIANGLE trial to examine rates of neurodiverse features and their associations with 18-month outcomes for patients and their carers. Patients (N = 370) enrolled in TRIANGLE completed baseline screening for autistic (AQ-10) and obsessive-compulsive features (OCI-R) and self-reported lifetime comorbid diagnoses. Patient and carer outcomes were measured at intervals up to 18 months. 27.1% of patients reported high autistic features, 61.6% reported high obsessive-compulsive features, and 21.7% reported high scores on both measures; 5.4% self-reported Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) diagnosis, and 16.2% self-reported Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) diagnosis. Patients with high autistic or obsessive-compulsive features had higher levels of eating and general psychopathology and poorer work and social adjustment at both baseline and 18 months later. However, those with high obsessive-compulsive characteristics had greater improvements on these outcomes over time. Carers of those with high autistic or obsessive-compulsive features reported similar caregiving skills and psychological distress at baseline. Over time, those supporting patients with high autistic features reported greater reductions in psychological distress. Those supporting patients with high obsessive-compulsive features reported greater improvements in caregiving skills. We observed high rates of neurodiversity in our large cohort of patients with AN, and in some cases, more robust improvement relative to those with lower scores on neurodiversity dimensions. Greater consideration of neurodiversity in AN treatment may enhance benefit for patients and carers.

title: Cross-Ancestry Polygenic Prediction of Bipolar Disorder and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder in India.
journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part B, Neuropsychiatric genetics : the official publication of the International Society of Psychiatric Genetics
abstract: Most genetic studies of psychiatric disorders have been conducted predominantly in populations of European ancestry, limiting evidence for the transferability of polygenic scores (PGS) to other populations. This cross-sectional study evaluated the predictive performance of European-derived PGS for bipolar disorder (BD) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in an Indian sample. Participants (N = 2531) included individuals with BD (N = 463), OCD (N = 554), and controls (N = 1514) recruited from hospital- and community-based samples. Genotyping was performed using the Illumina Global Screening Array. PGS were derived from the summary statistics of European-ancestry genome-wide association studies using two Bayesian methods, PRS-CS-auto and SBayesRC. Principal component analyses demonstrated genetic overlap of the study population with other South Asian populations. BD PGS showed significant predictive performance, explaining approximately 6%-7% of liability-scale variance with PGS-only AUCs of ~0.71. OCD PGS showed lower but significant predictive performance, explaining ~2%-3% of variance with AUCs of approximately 0.59. Bayesian approaches showed better predictive performance than conventional clumping-and-thresholding. These findings demonstrate that European-derived psychiatric PGS can retain predictive information in an Indian population, although performance differed between disorders. The application of Bayesian PGS methods in this Indian cohort supports their utility for cross-ancestry prediction, while reinforcing the need for larger genomic studies in South Asian and other underrepresented populations.

title: Accuracy of CSF tap test and lumbar infusion test in predicting shunt response in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) presents with gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary incontinence. The cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CSF-TT) and lumbar infusion test (LIT) are commonly used to predict postoperative improvement after shunt surgery; however, their validity remains debated. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the sensitivity and specificity of CSF-TT and LIT. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42023454502). Reporting followed the PRISMA-DTA guidelines, and the certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Of 1,955 studies, 15 were included, reporting on 721 CSF-TT and 393 LIT patients, with shunt surgery as the reference standard. Nine CSF-TT studies (n = 700) and five LIT studies (n = 368) contributed to the primary meta-analysis. Considerable heterogeneity existed in test protocols, timing of assessment, and outcome measures. Several studies were retrospective with a high risk of bias. The pooled estimates were derived from a limited number of heterogeneous studies. Using a bivariate random-effects model, pooled sensitivity and specificity of CSF-TT were 64.1% (95% CI 49.2-76.6%, I 2 81.3%) and 54.8% (95% CI 41.8-67.2%, I 2 59.7%), respectively. The certainty of evidence was very low for sensitivity due to bias, inconsistency, and imprecision, and low for poor specificity due to bias and inconsistency. LIT showed a pooled sensitivity of 77.5% (95% CI 70.2-83.4%, I 2 14.7%) and a specificity of 28.3% (95% CI 19.0-39.9%, I 2 4.6%), with moderate certainty for sensitivity and moderate certainty for poor specificity. Both CSF-TT and LIT show poor specificity for predicting shunt responsiveness in iNPH, with low-certainty evidence for CSF-TT and moderate-certainty evidence for LIT. A positive result from either test should not be used in isolation to guide surgical decisions. Standardized prospective studies with clearly defined patient selection criteria and outcome measures are needed to establish the true diagnostic value of these tests. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42023454502.

title: Deep brain stimulation in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a well-established treatment for neurological disorders, but its efficacy and safety in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain uncertain. This narrative review synthesizes nine clinical trials in patients with mild to severe AD, focusing on stimulation of the fornix, nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), and ventral capsule/ventral striatum. Literature was identified through PubMed using the terms "deep brain stimulation" and "Alzheimer's disease," and the results were restricted to clinical trials and case reports in English, with additional references identified through Google Scholar. Across studies, DBS was safe and well tolerated, with few adverse events. Stimulation produced short-term cognitive improvements, most commonly measured by Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale cognitive subscale, along with transient reversal of glucose hypometabolism and activation of memory-related networks. One study reported slowed hippocampal atrophy, suggesting neuroplastic effects. In severe AD, DBS targeting both the fornix and NBM yielded transient cognitive gains, with NBM-DBS showing greater benefit for neuropsychiatric symptoms and caregiver burden. Patients with higher baseline cognition and glucose metabolism responded more favorably to DBS. Age-related differences emerged: younger patients (<65 years old), with earlier onset and more aggressive progression, showed less favorable responses to DBS targeting the fornix, whereas older patients (≥65 years old) had comparatively better outcomes. Despite these benefits, DBS does not halt disease progression or reverse AD pathology. Larger, biomarker-stratified, sham-controlled trials with extended follow-up are needed to clarify durability, identify optimal patient subgroups, and determine the most effective stimulation targets.

title: A redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulation: a hypothesis on NLRP3-Mediated regulation.
abstract: Ovulation is a highly coordinated biological process involving endocrine regulation, tissue remodeling, immune activation, metabolic adaptation, and redox signaling. Although inflammatory responses are recognized as essential components of follicular rupture, the mechanisms integrating oxidative stress, metabolic alterations, and inflammasome activation during ovulatory progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we propose a hypothesis-driven redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulatory regulation, in which NLRP3 inflammasome signaling may serve as an important integrator of redox and metabolic cues that modulate inflammatory remodeling during the periovulatory period. This model suggests that successful ovulation requires a precisely balanced inflammatory threshold, whereas insufficient or excessive inflammasome activation may disrupt follicular homeostasis and contribute to ovarian dysfunction. Importantly, NLRP3 is proposed not as an indispensable determinant of follicular rupture, but as one regulatory component within a complex network involving cytokines, prostaglandins, matrix metalloproteinases, immune cells, and hormonal signals. By integrating current evidence linking mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, metabolic stress, and inflammation, this hypothesis provides a conceptual framework for understanding ovulation as a redox-sensitive immune-metabolic process. Future studies using cell type-specific NLRP3 manipulation, quantitative redox analysis, and single-cell approaches will be required to determine the physiological contribution of inflammasome signaling to ovulatory regulation.

title: Privacy-preserving synthetic data from a national CIDP registry: validation against real-world evidence.
abstract: Research in chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP) is constrained by low prevalence, limited data sharing, and privacy regulations. Disease registries mitigate some of these barriers, yet the reuse of individual-level data remains challenging. Artificial intelligence- and regression-based synthetic data (SD) generation may offer a privacy-preserving solution, provided analytical validity is maintained. We aimed to validate SD derived from the Italian CIDP Registry using a published case-control study as a reference framework. We analyzed a matched case-control dataset including 195 CIDP cases and 195 controls to examine lifestyle and dietary factors associated with CIDP risk. SD were generated using sequential conditional models stratified by sex. Fidelity was assessed by comparing real and SD in terms of marginal distributions, data distinguishability (propensity score mean squared error), and preservation of associations with CIDP risk using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. SD preserved the original case-control balance and sex distribution. Marginal distributions showed high concordance between real and SD, with minor smoothing in a small number of multi-level dietary variables. Distinguishability analyses indicated low separability between real and synthetic records. Univariable associations with CIDP risk were closely replicated, including the protective effects of higher fish and rice intake. Multivariable models demonstrated highly concordant effect estimates between datasets. SD derived from the Italian CIDP Registry accurately reproduces key analytical properties of real-world data while preserving patient privacy. This approach enables reproducible and shareable CIDP research and may support future applications, including synthetic standard-of-care comparator cohorts and precision medicine-oriented investigations.

title: The cost of mentalizing: executive contributions to social cognition performance in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
abstract: Mentalizing deficits are common in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Performance at high-level socio-cognitive tasks may be particularly vulnerable to integrity of basic cognitive processes. However, the extent to which non-social functioning contributes to socio-cognitive impairment in ALS remains poorly understood. In this study, we addressed this question in a large cohort of patients. We assessed 257 ALS patients and 120 healthy controls using the Story-based Empathy Task (SET), which dissociates intention attribution (IA), emotion attribution (EA), and basic causal inference (CI). Vectorial analyses were applied to quantify overall performance and imbalance between social and non-social components. Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the contribution of executive system integrity to social cognition performance in ALS. Patients showed significantly reduced performance across all SET conditions compared to controls, with imbalance between mentalizing and basic causal inference. Distinct profiles emerged across ALS phenotypes. ALS patients with behavioral changes exhibited predominant deficits in emotion attribution, whereas cognitively unimpaired ALS showed selective impairment in intention attribution. Executive functioning was significantly associated with SET performances and mediated the relationship between basic inference and both intention and emotion attribution. Mentalizing impairment in ALS reflects an interaction between executive processes and specialized socio-cognitive systems. The identification of dissociable profiles supports a dual-route, network-based model of ALS, involving socio-affective and inferential pathways, and underscores the importance of integrated cognitive assessment and more targeted interventions addressing both social and non-social cognitive domains.

title: Serotonergic regulation of neuronal excitability and glutamatergic synaptic transmission in rat claustrum.
abstract: The claustrum (CLA) receives dense serotonergic innervation from dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonin (5-HT) neurons, which are implicated in regulating sleep and stress homeostasis. However, the mechanisms by which 5-HT regulates the excitability of CLA neurons remain poorly defined. In the present study, we combined whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, 5-HT uncaging, and receptor pharmacology to examine the effects of 5-HT on the excitability of CLA neurons and their glutamatergic synapses. We found that 5-HT consistently induced membrane hyperpolarization or depolarization in regular-spiking type I and type II neurons, whereas it predominantly induced hyperpolarization in strongly adapting CLA neurons. The 5-HT-induced membrane hyperpolarization and depolarization were mediated by 5-HT1A receptors (5-HT1ARs) and 5-HT2A receptors (5-HT2ARs), respectively. Furthermore, we showed that activation of presynaptic 5-HT2ARs inhibits glutamatergic synaptic transmission in the CLA by reducing glutamate release. This effect was not mediated by the canonical phospholipase C (PLC) signaling cascade. Collectively, these findings reveal cell type-specific and multifaceted serotonergic modulation of the intrinsic excitability and synaptic transmission in the claustrum.

title: Beyond cell replacement: restoring organelle homeostasis as the next frontier of regenerative medicine.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) have traditionally been viewed as disorders driven by individual pathological processes, including protein aggregation, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, impaired autophagy, and neuroinflammation. However, growing evidence demonstrates that these mechanisms are not isolated events but interconnected manifestations of disrupted intracellular organelle communication. Dynamic interactions among mitochondria, the ER, lysosomes, peroxisomes, and other organelles coordinate calcium signaling, bioenergetics, proteostasis, lipid metabolism, and cellular stress adaptation, thereby preserving neuronal homeostasis. Progressive disruption of this communication network represents a fundamental driver of neuronal dysfunction and degeneration, suggesting that restoration of organelle homeostasis may constitute a more effective therapeutic strategy than targeting individual molecular pathways. In parallel, regenerative medicine has evolved beyond the concept of cell replacement toward approaches that enhance the resilience and repair capacity of surviving cells. Among these, mesenchymal stem cell (MSC)-derived secretomes and extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as promising cell-free therapeutics owing to their diverse repertoire of proteins, lipids, metabolites, cytokines, growth factors, and regulatory RNAs capable of simultaneously modulating multiple cellular pathways. Accumulating evidence indicates that these bioactive cargos modulate mitochondrial function, alleviate ER stress, improve autophagy-lysosomal activity, reduce oxidative stress and neuroinflammation, and reinforce proteostasis, collectively promoting intracellular homeostasis. Here, we propose organelle homeostasis as a promising focus for regenerative medicine and discuss how cell-free therapies may redefine therapeutic strategies for NDs by restoring the intracellular communication networks that sustain cellular resilience. Finally, we highlight current translational challenges and future opportunities for engineering next-generation cell-free therapeutics targeting complex diseases.

title: Clinicians' perspectives on complementary and alternative medicine use in headache care across Africa and West Asia: a cross-sectional survey.
abstract: Headache disorders impose a substantial burden across Africa and West Asia, where limited access to healthcare may increase reliance on complementary and alternative medicine (CAM). The current study explored clinicians' perspectives on CAM use, safety concerns, and research needs across countries with different income status. A cross-sectional web-based survey of 123 neurologists and headache specialists with at least 5 years of experience in headache management from 37 countries was carried out. They were classified into Low/Lower-Middle Income Countries (LIC/LMIC) and Upper-Middle Income Countries/High Income Countries (UMIC/HIC) groups in accordance with the World Bank income classifications. Of 123 participants (median age 42 years; 50.4% males), 52.8% were from LICs/LMICs. Clinicians reported that CAMs were frequently used in both groups, and there was no significant difference in overall frequency of CAM use (p = 0.116). Clinicians in both groups perceived migraine as the most common headache type for which patients used CAM. However, significant differences in CAM modalities were observed. Acupuncture (79.3% vs. 47.7%, p < 0.001), massage (86.2% vs. 63.1%, p = 0.004), yoga (56.9% vs. 20.0%, p < 0.001), and supplements (93.1% vs. 66.2%, p < 0.001) were reported by the clinicians as significantly higher in UMICs/HICs, whereas spiritual healing was significantly higher in LICs/LMICs (70.8% vs. 46.6%, p = 0.006). Clinicians reported that patients in LICs/LMICs were significantly more likely to consult CAM prior to seeking medical care (89.2% vs. 67.2%, p = 0.003), and perceived cost as a major factor influencing CAM use (81.5% vs. 27.6%, p < 0.001). CAM appears to be commonly encountered in headache care across Africa and West Asia according to clinician reports. Although its use is shaped by cultural beliefs, accessibility, and perceived safety, concerns over unregulated products, herb-drug interactions, and delayed conventional medical treatments were also highlighted.

title: Neurobehavioral dysregulation, depressive symptoms, and cognition in former American football players.
abstract: Neurobehavioral dysregulation (NBD) is a core clinical feature of traumatic encephalopathy syndrome (TES), but its relationships with repetitive head impact (RHI) exposure, cognitive performance, and depressive symptoms remain unclear. This study examined clinical factors associated with NBD among former American football players with substantial RHI exposure. Cross-sectional baseline data were analyzed from 179 former American football players enrolled in the DIAGNOSE CTE Research Project, including 119 former professional and 60 former college players. NBD was assessed using measures of impulsivity, behavioral regulation, hostility, and emotional lability. Multivariate regression models evaluated associations of continuous NBD scores with depressive symptom dimensions, cognitive performance, playing level, and years of football participation, adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates. Secondary analyses evaluated dichotomized NBD outcomes using study-specific thresholds. Bonferroni-adjusted p-values were reported for multiple comparisons. Depressive symptoms demonstrated the most consistent associations with NBD. Greater neurovegetative depressive symptom burden was associated with greater impulsivity (estimate = 6.84; 95% CI = 4.45, 9.23; p-value < 0.0001), behavioral dysregulation (estimate = 11.63; 95% CI = 8.50, 14.76; p-value < 0.0001), hostility (estimate = 5.07; 95% CI = 2.32, 7.81; p-value = 0.0004), and emotional lability (estimate = 1.16; 95% CI = 0.12, 2.20; p-value = 0.0284). Greater agitated/reactive depressive symptom burden was associated with greater impulsivity (estimate = 3.42; 95% CI = 1.44, 5.41; p-value = 0.0008) and hostility (estimate = 5.11; 95% CI = 2.89, 7.32; p-value < 0.0001), while greater affective depressive symptom burden was associated with greater behavioral dysregulation (estimate = 3.09; 95% CI = 0.01, 6.18; p-value = 0.0494). Better verbal memory was associated with lower impulsivity (estimate = -2.02; 95% CI = -3.65, -0.40; p-value = 0.0149) and behavioral dysregulation (estimate = -2.64; 95% CI = -4.76, -0.52; p-value = 0.0150), while better executive speed was associated with lower behavioral dysregulation (estimate = -3.10; 95% CI = -5.11, -1.09; p-value = 0.0027). Years of football exposure was not independently associated with NBD outcomes. Among former American football players with substantial RHI exposure, depressive symptom burden was more consistently associated with NBD than football participation characteristics or cognitive performance. These findings support a heterogeneous clinical phenotype and underscore the importance of evaluating depressive symptoms when interpreting NBD in the context of TES.

title: Inscribed and expendable: oncological trauma, body memory, and the politics of grievability in Anne Boyer's The Undying.
abstract: The study examines the thematic resonances and disjunctions between Medical Humanities, Trauma Studies, and Feminist Critical Theory through a close reading of Anne Boyer's Pulitzer Prize-winning pathography The Undying. The research argues that the bodies of female cancer patients experience, remember, and resist oncological violence in contrast to late-capitalist biomedical discourse. Drawing on Bessel van der Kolk's clinical account of implicit, non-declarative body memory, understood here not as a diagnostic claim about Boyer's neurobiology but as a way of reading literary form, the study reads Boyer's syntactically fragmented, recursive prose as both a figuration of chemotherapy-induced somatic violation and a formal strategy to represent what testimony cannot. Judith Butler's analytics of precarity and grievability are essential to this inquiry, illuminating the role of normative biopolitical regimes in allocating institutional protection, therapeutic resources, and public mourning along intersectional axes of gender, ethnicity, and class, rendering certain oncological bodies structurally non-grievable. This reading of the biopolitical investments conditioned by cancer and by its differential histories is further underscored by the World Health Organization's Global Breast Cancer Initiative and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 3 imperative that oncological treatment be gender equitable and that by 2030 deaths from non-communicable diseases be substantially reduced. Within this context, Boyer's feminist micro-narratives of somatic trauma, chemotherapeutic toxicity, and institutional abandonment stand in transnational epidemiological and humanistic urgency.

title: Safe and efficient intracellular delivery of functional antibodies into cultured neural cells shows a role for Alzheimer's-relevant tau phosphorylation in cell integrity.
abstract: Protein proteoforms generated by post-translational modification are increasingly recognized as important regulators of neuronal function and neurodegenerative disease. However, methods for acutely interrogating specific intracellular proteoforms in living neuronal populations remain limited. We evaluated cationic liposomal delivery (CLD) as a strategy for introducing full-length functional antibodies into living neurons and used this approach to investigate the role of a phosphorylated tau proteoform recognized by the monoclonal antibody PHF-1. Cationic liposomes composed of DOPC+ were complexed with antibodies or molecular probes and applied to cultured neuronal cell lines and primary mouse cortical neurons. Intracellular delivery, cellular localization, viability, and biological activity were assessed using fluorescence microscopy and live-cell imaging. CLD efficiently delivered full-length antibodies and molecular probes into living neuronal cells and primary neurons without detectable toxicity. Internalized antibodies retained target specificity, producing intracellular staining patterns consistent with the known localization of tau, vinculin, paxillin, and Fyn. Delivery was observed across essentially all cells in treated cultures and remained effective under standard culture conditions. Intracellular delivery of PHF-1 produced a rapid and striking morphological response characterized by neurite retraction and cell-body rounding within hours of treatment. These effects were not observed with heat-inactivated PHF-1, vehicle controls, or other intracellular antibodies, supporting a specific effect of intracellular engagement of PHF-1-reactive tau species. These findings establish CLD as a practical platform for the intracellular delivery of functional full-length antibodies into living neuronal populations. Beyond validating a delivery technology, the study demonstrates that acute intracellular engagement of PHF-1-reactive phosphorylated tau rapidly alters neuronal morphology, suggesting that this tau proteoform contributes to the maintenance of neurite integrity. CLD provides a versatile approach for probing the function of intracellular proteoforms that are difficult to study using conventional genetic or biochemical methods.

title: Understanding the impact of unmet needs on the health and wellbeing of people with stroke, living in the community: a scoping review of reviews.
abstract: Recovery from stroke may often be incomplete, with unresolved issues persisting as unmet needs. However, the impact of these needs on both the health and wellbeing of people with stroke, subgroups, and their carers remains unclear. This scoping review of reviews aimed to provide an overview of evidence on unmet needs and their impact on the wellbeing of people living in the community with stroke. Relevant databases (14) were searched from 2,000 onwards and included systematic, scoping, and umbrella reviews meeting criteria related to population, concept, and context, and reporting quantitative and/or qualitative data. Over 620 studies (including repeated studies across reviews) and 3.5 million participants were described in 28 eligible reviews. The needs and impacts were wide-ranging for the population as a whole and for sub-groups, e.g., with specific impairments (communication issues) or demographics (younger people who may have had a stroke or people who are culturally and linguistically diverse). No one framework covers the diversity of impacts on health and wellbeing-physical, emotional, and psychological health, as well as issues of relationships, inclusion, engagement, meaning, cultural and spiritual needs, financial, and other environmental domains. Our findings provide important, often ignored insights and direction for people with stroke generally, as well as sub-groups. Ultimately, services and research should operate at multiple levels and address quality-of-life impacts, including social integration, sense of self, and life purpose. Review protocol registration: https://osf.io/efut8/.

title: Burnout pathway differences across dual-track residency training: a network analysis.
abstract: China's standardized residency training operates under a dual-track system: one track integrates clinical training with concurrent degree pursuit (student group), while the other is purely vocational without degree conferral (non-student group). Prior burnout research has largely relied on aggregate total or subscale scores, which cannot detect qualitative differences in symptom-to-symptom connectivity even when mean burnout severity is similar. Despite identical clinical rotations and competency requirements, it remains unclear whether these structurally distinct training pathways are associated with different burnout symptom-connectivity patterns, with direct implications for track-specific educational support. We conducted a secondary analysis of data from Fan et al.'s previously published cross-sectional survey of 636 residents from a Chinese tertiary teaching hospital. Burnout was measured using the 22-item Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS). Networks were estimated using Graphical Lasso, and bridge centrality was computed to identify symptoms that most strongly connect burnout dimensions. Analyses were stratified by gender and specialty, and supplemented by logistic regression and bootstrap resampling. Non-students showed higher emotional exhaustion and lower personal accomplishment scores than students, whereas depersonalization scores did not differ significantly between groups. Burnout prevalence was higher among non-students (50.2% vs. 42.4%), but this difference was not statistically significant. In both groups, DP2 ("I don't really care what happens to patients") was the dominant bridge node. However, PA4 ("I don't easily understand how my patients feel") entered the top five bridge items only in non-students. Three of four subgroups followed the DP2 pathway, whereas non-student males showed a distinct pattern with PA4 as the most prominent feature (BS = 1.445). Logistic regression found no significant association between training identity and burnout status after adjustment (OR = 1.07; ΔAUC = +0.002, p = 0.68), whereas network analyses revealed distinct symptom-connectivity patterns. These findings suggest that burnout prevention should account for training structure and institutional context. Rather than uniform wellness programs, medical education should offer track-specific support, particularly for residents whose burnout is characterized by empathy-related frustration rather than depersonalization.

title: Prehospital Analgesia in Trauma: A Systematic Review of Current Evidence.
abstract: Pain management is integral to prehospital trauma care. However, due to multiple challenges, pain is frequently undertreated despite important physiologic and psychologic implications. Among these challenges is uncertainty regarding the safety and effectiveness of pharmacologic agents administered enroute. We aimed to evaluate the level of evidence for the safety and effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adult trauma patients. An electronic database search of PUBMED, Google Scholar, Cochrane Library, Embase and Scopus for studies that reported on safety and/or effectiveness of prehospital pharmacologic analgesia for acutely injured adults (aged > 15 years) from January 1st, 2014, to January 1st, 2026. Non-original studies, paediatric studies, studies of non-pharmacologic agents or non-systemic administration (e.g., topical) were excluded. Seventeen studies, involving 17,115 patients, met the inclusion criteria. The studies consisted of 6 randomized controlled trials, 5 retrospective cohort studies, one retrospective comparative study, one retrospective observational study, two prospective observational studies, one prospective cohort study and one non-randomized clinical trial. Agents included opioids, ketamine, methoxyflurane and paracetamol. Apart from one study of opioid therapy, no drug-attributed serious adverse events were reported. Minor adverse effects such as nausea, dizziness, dysphoria, agitation and drowsiness were common. All agents demonstrated effectiveness to varying levels. Current evidence demonstrates an overall favourable safety and effectiveness profile of prehospital analgesia for adult trauma patients. However, considering the wide prehospital prevalence of injury-related pain, evidence is limited by scope, methodology and variations of treatment protocols.

title: Suppressing the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway rescues pink1 deficiency in Drosophila and influences mitochondrial morphology.
abstract: Sterol-regulatory element binding proteins (SREBP) are master transcriptional factors controlling lipogenesis. In Drosophila, the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway is essential for development. Homozygous SREBP mutants are lipid deficient and larval lethal, whereas excessive lipids in flies are often associated with neurodegeneration. Since SREBP has previously been identified as a risk factor for Parkinson's disease, we further investigated the role of SREBP-mediated lipogenesis in a pink1 deficient Drosophila parkinsonism model. We found that expressing either dominant negative SREBP or knocking down its downstream target rescues pink1 mutant phenotypes including thorax indentation and impaired locomotion. Investigation of the indirect flight muscles reveals that suppression of the lipogenic pathway restores defective muscle morphology and mitochondrial defects, and reduces ectopic ROS associated with the pink1 null allele. Interestingly, we found altered mitochondrial morphologies when the lipogenic pathway was manipulated under physiological condition, suggesting the SREBP-mediated lipogenic pathway plays a role in regulating mitochondrial shapes. Our findings highlight the tight connection between lipid metabolism and mitochondria in both disease and physiological setting.

title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto-Viscoelastic Patches.
abstract: We report a machine learning (ML)-augmented magnetic sensing system for real-time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″-Fe16N2 microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML-based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical-grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real-time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

title: A comparison of different measures of the soleus Ia-motoneuron pathway in people with incomplete spinal cord injury.
abstract: Measures of the Ia-motoneuron pathway, including ratio of the maximum H-reflex and M-wave (Hmax/Mmax), rate-dependent depression of H-reflex (RDD) and clonus, are often used to quantify hyperreflexia after spinal cord injury (SCI). However, conflicting reports exist regarding the effect of SCI on these measures. In addition, the reliability of these measures is unknown for people with SCI. This study explored the potential effects of group (SCI or Control), age and sex, on Hmax/Mmax, RDD and clonus, as well as the reliability of each measure. Fifteen individuals with motor-incomplete SCI and 18 uninjured participants completed the study. All measures were recorded twice on two separate days. Reliability was quantified by the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient. Effects of group and age were explored by Linear Mixed Models or non-parametric methods as appropriate. Compared to Controls, those with SCI showed less RDD (Mann-Whitney U=-130, p=0.001) and more clonus (LMM Group main effect p=0.005), but no difference in Hmax/Mmax. In Controls, Sex affected the Hmax/Mmax (LMM main effect p<0.001), with females showing higher values than males. The small number of female SCI participants made it impossible to explore sex differences after SCI. In those with SCI, the test-retest reliability was moderate for the Hmax/Mmax and clonus, but low for RDD, suggesting reliability should be considered when comparing the changes of these measurements over time. Potential age and sex differences in Hmax/Mmax may have contributed to conflicting reports in the past.

title: Ekbom Spectrum Psychosis Associated with 24-hour Continuous Subcutaneous Foslevodopa/Foscarbidopa Infusion in Parkinson's Disease.
journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Continuous subcutaneous foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion (CSFLI) is an emerging treatment for advanced Parkinson's disease (PD). We report atypical psychosis with Ekbom-like somatic hallucinations during CSFLI. A 74-year-old man with a 16-year history of PD (Hoehn and Yahr stage 3), mild cognitive impairment (Montreal Cognitive Assessment 25/30), and previous mild dopamine agonist-induced visual hallucinations received CSFLI for disabling motor fluctuations, dyskinesias, nocturnal rigidity, and severe morning akinesia inadequately controlled by oral therapy. Initial treatment was well tolerated, reducing OFF time, dyskinesias, and sleep disturbance. Because of recurrent motor fluctuations and nocturnal akinesia, infusion parameters were progressively increased to a daytime base rate of 0.48 ml/h and a nocturnal low-rate of 0.38 ml/h, corresponding to an estimated levodopa equivalent daily dose of approximately 1,868 mg/day. Seventy-two hours after ciprofloxacin initiation for an infected subcutaneous nodule, the patient developed vivid visual hallucinations that evolved into Ekbom-like somatic hallucinations, described as worms moving beneath the skin, leading to superficial self-inflicted lacerations. Orientation remained preserved and no delirium features were observed. Initial reduction of infusion parameters, safinamide discontinuation, and quetiapine produced only partial benefit. A subsequent selective reduction of the nocturnal low-rate from 0.36 to 0.30 ml/h was associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in psychotic symptoms, although residual hallucinations and worsening morning akinesia persisted. This case suggests that psychosis during CSFLI may reflect the interaction between neuropsychiatric vulnerability, ciprofloxacin exposure, and sustained nocturnal dopaminergic stimulation. Although causality cannot be inferred, careful nocturnal titration may help clinicians recognize and manage atypical psychotic manifestations early in susceptible patients.

title: Probing the Effect of Mindfulness Training on Glutamate/GABA Ratio and Its Association with Dopamine Availability: A Preliminary Single-arm Pilot Study.
journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Mindfulness is an effective non-pharmacological intervention for mental health. However, little is known about the underlying neurological mechanisms involved, especially glutamate, γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), and the excitation-inhibition (E-I) balance. This study examined changes in these markers after mindfulness training and whether these changes are related to the baseline dopamine transporter (DAT) availability. We also probed the associations with outcome markers of mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) training. In this single-arm pilot study, 11 participants with Graves' disease were enrolled and received MBSR training. Single-photon emission computed tomography study using [99mTc]TRODAT-1 was employed to assess DAT availability before the intervention, and 1H magnetic resonance spectroscopy was used to assess the concentrations of glutamate, GABA, and the E-I balance. Attention and heart rate variability (HRV) were also measured before/after MBSR training. An elevated E-I balance and reduced GABA concentration after MBSR training were found. A lower baseline DAT availability was associated with a greater increase in glutamate and a greater increase in the E-I balance. A greater E-I balance after training was related to a greater frequency of HRV and better attention performance after the intervention. The findings are novel. An elevated E-I balance could be the short-term effect of MBSR training, and this effect was greater among participants with a lower level of DAT availability at baseline. This finding may imply that excitation-related processes, such as neuroplasticity, could be the overlooked mechanism of mindfulness training.

title: Altered NCAM1, NRXN1, NLGN4, and CDH2 Levels in Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Their Unaffected Siblings.
journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been increasingly associated with alterations in synaptic function and plasticity, in which cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) play a critical role. This study aimed to compare peripheral levels of NCAM1, NRXN1, NLGN4, and CDH2 among individuals with ASD, their unaffected siblings, and healthy controls, and to examine their associations with autism severity and autistic traits in siblings. The study included 41 children aged 18-72 months diagnosed with ASD according to DSM-5 criteria, 41 unaffected siblings of children with ASD (control group 1, aged 24-72 months), and 41 typically developing children (control group 2, aged 18-72 months). The severity of ASD symptoms was evaluated using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale and the Autism Behavior Checklist. Parents of the siblings completed the Autism Spectrum Screening Questionnaire to assess subclinical autistic traits. Serum NCAM1, NRXN1, NLGN4, and CDH2 levels were measured in peripheral blood samples using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. No statistically significant differences were observed among the study groups in serum levels of NCAM1, NRXN1, NLGN4, or CDH2. However, within the ASD group, a significant positive correlation was found between NCAM1 and NRXN1 levels, suggesting a potential interrelation between these synaptic adhesion molecules. Although peripheral levels of NCAM1, NRXN1, NLGN4, and CDH2 did not differ among groups, the observed molecular correlation in ASD cases may reflect subtle mechanisms influencing synaptic connectivity. Further biochemical and genetic studies are warranted to clarify the roles of these molecules in the etiology and neurobiology of ASD.

title: Reduced Serum Apelin-13 Levels in Medication-free Adults with Major Depressive Disorder.
journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: The apelinergic system has been implicated in neuroinflammatory and neuroplastic mechanisms related to depressive disorders. Apelin-13, the most biologically active isoform of apelin, has demonstrated antidepressant-like effects in preclinical studies; however, clinical evidence remains limited. This study aimed to investigate serum Apelin-13 levels in medication-free adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) and assess their clinical relevance. This cross-sectional, case-control study included 80 medication-free adults diagnosed with MDD and 81 healthy control subjects matched for age, sex, and body mass index. Psychiatric diagnoses were established using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5. Depression severity was assessed using the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. Serum Apelin-13 concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Between-group comparisons, correlation analyses, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses, and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed. Serum Apelin-13 levels were significantly lower in patients with MDD than in healthy controls (p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis demonstrated a moderate discriminative ability of serum Apelin-13 levels, with an area under the curve of 0.719. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that lower serum Apelin-13 levels were independently associated with MDD after adjustment for relevant confounding variables (p < 0.001). No significant association was observed between serum Apelin-13 levels and depression severity. These findings indicate that serum Apelin-13 levels are reduced in medication-free adults with MDD and may reflect an underlying biological vulnerability rather than current symptom severity. Apelin-13 may represent a trait-related biomarker contributing to the biological characterization of depressive disorders.

title: The Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) and the Five Aggregates (skandha-s) of the Early Buddhism: Parallels and Differences on Understanding of Human Mind.
journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: The research domain criteria (RDoC) was launched by the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) to provide a framework towards development of neurobiological models and novel treatment methods for mental health disorders. Here we elucidate the possible parallels between the RDoC and the understanding of human mind by the early Buddhism, conceptualized as the five aggregates (skandha-s). They both define the function of human mind as a collective operation of de-centralized systems. The state-of-art neuroscience and the long tradition of empirical observation and practice of introspection converges on human mind as division into dimensional sub-sets that can sometime coordinate but often do not. We argue that this similarity not only brings academic interest, but also clinical and practical purposes of incorporating the theoretical framework and empirical data of the early Buddhism into the daily execution of tools originated from this tradition, including the mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs).

title: An Update on Xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) for Schizophrenia: Emerging Evidence and Clinical Implications.
journal: Clinical psychopharmacology and neuroscience : the official scientific journal of the Korean College of Neuropsychopharmacology
abstract: Xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) is a novel treatment for schizophrenia that exerts its therapeutic benefit through muscarinic receptors without direct dopamine receptor effect. Xanomeline is a muscarinic M1- and M4-preferring receptor agonist, while trospium acts as a peripherally acting muscarinic antagonist that mitigates cholinergic adverse effects without crossing the blood-brain barrier. Since our initial publication in this journal reviewing data from the EMERGENT clinical trials, additional evidence has emerged that further characterizes the efficacy, safety, and clinical role of xanomeline-trospium in schizophrenia. This review provides an overview of recent evidence. Across pooled analyses of randomized trials, xanomeline-trospium demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements in positive, negative, cognitive, and agitation-related symptoms, with treatment effects observed as early as week 2 on some measures. Benefits were observed in patients with prominent negative symptoms, greater cognitive impairment, and higher levels of agitation at baseline. Long-term open-label studies demonstrated sustained improvement in symptoms and tolerability over 52 weeks among both previously treated and treatment-naïve patients, supporting findings from the 5-week EMERGENT trials. Improvements in functional impairment were also reported. Xanomeline-trospium was well tolerated, with gastrointestinal adverse effects occurring more frequently than placebo, while rates of extrapyramidal symptoms, clinically meaningful weight gain, and metabolic disturbances were low and comparable to or lower than placebo. Indirect comparisons to antipsychotics further suggested favorable benefit to risk profile. These findings provide continued support of xanomeline-trospium as an effective and well-tolerated treatment for schizophrenia. Future research is needed to assess the effectiveness of xanomeline-trospium across different stages of schizophrenia and through head-to-head trials.

title: EXPRESS: Multidomain determinants of perivascular spaces indicate early cerebrovascular vulnerability in individuals at risk of Alzheimer's disease.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
abstract: Perivascular spaces (PVS) are MRI-visible markers of cerebrovascular and glymphatic function, but their regional determinants in preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD), regarding sex and AD biomarkers, remain poorly understood. We studied 1,199 cognitively unimpaired ALFA study participants (aged 54-65 years), genetically enriched for AD risk, with CSF biomarker phenotyping in 296 participants. PVS were automatically quantified in basal ganglia, centrum semiovale, hippocampus, and midbrain on 3T MRI. Counts were modelled using Poisson or negative binomial regression, adjusting for demographics, cardiometabolic, lifestyle, and genetic factors, with effect modification by sex and amyloid/tau (AT) status. PVS showed marked regional specificity. Centrum semiovale PVS were associated with age, male sex, and cardiometabolic factors, whereas hippocampal and midbrain PVS were more closely related to AD biomarker status and sleep or psychological measures. Men exhibited higher centrum semiovale burden while women showed higher counts in hippocampus, midbrain, and basal ganglia. Associations were stronger in amyloid-positive individuals with concurrent tau pathology. Polygenic scores for lipid and metabolic traits contributed modestly to regional PVS variation. PVS burden is associated with multidomain determinants in preclinical AD with regional, sex-specific, and biomarker-dependent patterns, supporting PVS as accessible MRI markers for risk stratification and precision prevention.

title: EXPRESS: The function of microRNAs transported by cell extracellular vesicles in post-stroke recovery: a systematic review.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
abstract: Stroke is associated with persistently elevated rates of mortality and disability. Effective cerebroprotection strategies and interventions for promoting functional recovery after stroke remain an unmet need. Cell transplantation represents a potential therapeutic strategy for facilitating brain recovery and regeneration. Its therapeutic benefits are thought to be partly mediated by extracellular vesicles and the various miRNAs they carry, which from different cell sources may exert distinct therapeutic effects. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library for original studies on extracellular vesicles in post-stroke recovery, focusing on miRNA mechanisms. Data on cell source, miRNA, in vitro/vivo model, administration, target/pathway, outcomes, and presumed treatment window were extracted. We categorize exosomal miRNAs into three distinct groups based on their cellular origins: mesenchymal stem cells, other stem cells, and non-stem cells. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles carry diverse miRNAs regulating angiogenesis, inflammation, apoptosis, autophagy, and neuroplasticity; other stem cell-derived vesicles show source-specific effects; non-stem cell-derived vesicles from astrocytes, microglia, and endothelial cells also modulate neuronal survival and repair. Therapeutic effects span acute cytoprotection, subacute tissue repair, and chronic neuroplasticity. Most miRNAs are supported by at least one in vivo study, while a few rely mainly on in vitro evidence.

title: Reduced Sensory Attenuation Scales with Tic Severity in Tourette Syndrome.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
abstract: Patients with Tourette syndrome (TS) often describe tics as reactions to uncomfortable somatic sensations (premonitory urges), suggesting a breakdown in how the brain filters internally generated sensory information. This filtering capacity is indexed by sensory attenuation (SA), a mechanism relying on sensorimotor predictions to dampen the perceived intensity of self-produced inputs. However, objective behavioral evidence of such impairment in TS remains lacking. The aims were to determine whether patients with TS exhibit reduced SA and to evaluate whether the magnitude of this impairment correlates with the severity of the symptoms related to the syndrome. Thirty adults with TS and 30 healthy controls performed a force-matching task. Participants reproduced a target force in a direct condition (directly with their finger) and in an indirect condition (controlling force via a button). TS patients underwent a comprehensive clinical assessment, including the Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (YGTSS). Compared with controls, patients with TS exhibited reduced SA, evidenced by lower force overestimation during direct force reproduction, whereas no group differences were observed in the indirect condition. This reduction was associated with greater tic severity and accounted for additional variance in YGTSS total tic scores beyond medication load, obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and premonitory urge severity. These findings provide the first direct behavioral evidence of reduced SA in adults with TS. The observed association with tic severity suggests that SA may represent a clinically relevant behavioral marker of altered sensorimotor predictive processing in TS. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

title: New insights of oligodendrocytes in the etiology of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Oligodendrocytes (OLs) are myelin-forming cells in the central nervous system (CNS), providing nutritional and metabolic support to axons. They also interact with other glial cells to regulate the microenvironment of the CNS. Recent clinical studies have revealed that OL dysfunction and white matter changes occur at an early stage of Parkinson's disease (PD) and may be associated with dopaminergic neuronal damage, postural, and gait disorders. However, whether these changes are primary drivers or secondary consequences of neurodegeneration remains to be determined. Biochemical and genetic studies have provided evidence for OL dysfunction in PD pathology. Mechanistic studies have shown that OL damage can disrupt neuronal integrity through communicating with neurons, and the aggregation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) in OLs also accelerates dopaminergic neuronal death. Emerging evidence suggests that OLs may play a significant role in the pathogenesis and progression of PD through their involvement in mitochondrial damage, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. In this review, we summarized current understanding of oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs), OLs, myelination, and white matter in the pathogenesis of PD and discussed the potential therapy by targeting OLs for PD.

title: The Boron-Neuron Connection: The Potential of Boron-Containing Molecules for Treating Incurable Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
abstract: Boron (B), a group 13 metalloid, has emerged as a versatile element at the intersection of chemistry, biology, and medicine. Its electron-deficient nature and ability to reversibly interconvert between trigonal planar (sp2) and tetrahedral (sp3) geometries enable dynamic covalent interactions with biological nucleophiles, making boron-containing compounds (BCCs) attractive pharmacophores that selectively interact with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and are ROS-responsive for therapeutic development. BCCs possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metal-chelating properties that make them attractive candidates for neurodegenerative diseases. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a fatal and multifactorial motor neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metal dyshomeostasis, providing a strong rationale for exploring boron-based therapeutics. This review examines current literature on B chemistry, pharmacology, and translational applications, with emphasis on mechanisms relevant to ALS pathogenesis. This review focuses on ROS-responsive B scaffolds, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, neuroprotective mechanisms, hormonal modulation, metal chelation, and emerging preclinical evidence supporting boron-based interventions. BCCs represent a promising yet underexplored therapeutic platform for ALS and related neurodegenerative disorders. Their ROS-responsive, redox-modulating, and neuroprotective properties, combined with favorable CNS drug-like pharmacokinetics, offer a mechanistically distinct approach to disease modification. Emerging preclinical evidence strongly supports further translational investigation.

title: Electrovestibulography biomarkers differentiate schizophrenia from healthy controls: implications for the dopamine hypothesis.
journal: The world journal of biological psychiatry : the official journal of the World Federation of Societies of Biological Psychiatry
abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated that Electrovestibulography (EVestG) biomarkers for Parkinson's Disease are sensitive to dopamine levels. Given the dopamine hypothesis of Schizophrenia (SCZ), we recorded EVestG signals from 45 individuals with SCZ and 36 healthy controls to evaluate whether EVestG can differentiate these populations. Features derived from field potentials (FP) and firing pattern interval histograms (IH33)-the two primary EVestG outcomes-were extracted and used to classify the two groups. We achieved a 78% cross-validated accuracy using a Naïve Bayes classifier. This classification performance was achieved despite nearly all SCZ participants being on antipsychotic medications with most on high (n = 21) or partial (n = 4) dopamine D2 receptor affinity, which would be expected to attenuate the dopaminergic signal. The exploratory separation of SCZ the sub-groups on high (N = 15) and low affinity (N = 15) D2 medications was achieved for the FP feature (p = 0.027). Features derived from both static and dynamic segments of the EVestG signal were altered in SCZ; features from dynamic segments-which impose greater metabolic demand on the vestibular system-showed more pronounced group differences than those from static segments.

title: Does smartphone addiction exist? A critical evaluation of the validity of behavioural addiction symptoms in problematic smartphone use.
abstract: The current debate raises the question of whether "smartphone addiction" really exists and whether the phenomenon can be considered as a distinct, clinically relevant disorder. This question is examined from three perspectives: 1) the terminology and definition of the problematic behaviour, 2) the evidence of clinical relevance, the theoretical embedding and empirical robustness of negative consequences and related psychological mechanisms, and 3) a critical reflection of current measurement tools. The assumption that problematic smartphone use is a distinct behavioural addiction is not valid. Clear evidence for clinical relevance, the integration in theoretical framework models from addiction research, and a standardized definition and classification for deriving diagnostic criteria distinguishing the usage from other problematic behaviours and activities are needed. Therefore, we provide the following specific recommendations for future research: 1) investigating the clinical relevance of potential impairments solely due to smartphone use, which also includes a methodological paradigm shift; 2) focusing on a more comprehensive theoretical embedding for and against the addiction argumentation; 3) investigating underlying mechanisms by additionally considering smartphone-specific mechanisms (e.g., usage types, availability). Current evidence does not support problematic smartphone use as a distinct behavioural addiction. Future research should use more robust methods to clarify whether it can be conceptualised within the addiction framework or as an alternative mechanism or medium for a different type of disorder.

title: MUSIC-PD: A Delphi-Derived, Culturally Adaptable Music Therapy Protocol for Parkinson's Disease Rehabilitation.
abstract: Music-based interventions have shown promise in Parkinson's disease (PD) rehabilitation. However, variability in intervention design, delivery, dose, and documentation limits clinical translation. The aim of the study was to develop a consensus-based music therapy protocol for PD, designed to permit cultural and linguistic adaptation. A PRISMA-informed evidence-mapping review identified music-based and rhythm-based interventions relevant to PD rehabilitation. Findings informed a modified Delphi process involving a multidisciplinary expert panel of movement disorder neurologists, qualified music therapists, and people with PD. Round 1 generated qualitative inputs on therapeutic domains, safety, feasibility, and cultural adaptation. These were synthesized into 36 structured statements and rated in Round 2 using a 5-point Likert scale. Consensus was predefined as ≥80% agreement. The evidence map included 32 studies and identified 3 therapeutic clusters: motor/gait rehabilitation, voice-respiratory communication, and nonmotor cognitive-affective engagement. Of the 36 Delphi statements, 33 reached consensus. High-convergence domains included patient-preferred familiar music, cultural adaptation, rhythmic auditory stimulation for gait rehabilitation, multidomain symptom targeting, and vocal rehabilitation. The final framework was organized into LAYA-Locomotor Auditory Yielding Activation Module, NADA-Neurocognitive and Affective Domain Activation Module, and RAGA-Respiratory Aerodynamic Glottal Activation Module. The protocol incorporated session-selection rules, safety screening, difficulty levels, active and/or receptive therapy components, flexible pragmatic session guidance, caregiver-supported practice, and a proposed session-planning/documentation resource. MUSIC-PD provides a structured, Delphi-derived, and panel-approved framework for integrating music-based interventions into multidisciplinary PD rehabilitation. It translates evidence and multidisciplinary consensus into a protocol intended for prospective feasibility, fidelity, safety, and efficacy evaluation.

title: In Vitro and In Vivo Ocular Safety Assessment of Pexidartinib.
journal: Journal of ocular pharmacology and therapeutics : the official journal of the Association for Ocular Pharmacology and Therapeutics
abstract: Pexidartinib (PLX3397), a small-molecule kinase inhibitor, has shown therapeutic potential in experimental ocular inflammatory and retinal degenerative disease models following oral administration; however, its intravitreal (IVT) safety remains unknown. As IVT delivery enables direct retinal targeting, this study aims to evaluate the IVT safety profile of pexidartinib using in vitro and in vivo models. In vitro safety of pexidartinib was evaluated in adult retinal pigment epithelial cells (ARPE-19), 661W, human corneal epithelial (HCE), and N9 cell lines using the MTT assay. In vivo safety was assessed in rats following IVT administration of pexidartinib at 100 nM, 10 μM, and 100 μM. Ocular safety was evaluated using slit-lamp biomicroscopy, intraocular pressure (IOP) measurements, RT-qPCR, histology, and immunofluorescence. Pexidartinib was well tolerated in ARPE-19, 661W, HCE, and N9cells up to 10 μM, while higher concentrations (50-100 μM) reduced cell viability in all cell lines except in 661W cells. In vivo, slit-lamp examination and IOP measurements showed no detectable changes postinjection across all tested concentrations. Histological and immunofluorescence evaluation demonstrated preserved retinal and corneal layers, with no significant increase in retinal Caspase-3 expression. Furthermore, RT-qPCR analysis showed minor alterations, predominantly at the low dose (100 nM), compared with the higher doses (10 and 100 μM); however, these changes were not associated with structural or apoptotic degeneration, possibly indicating nonmonotonic dose responses for various kinase inhibitors. IVT pexidartinib was well tolerated in both in vitro (10 μM) and in vivo (100 μM). These findings support the potential development of pexidartinib as a localized therapy for treating posterior segment eye diseases. However, further long-term studies on ocular safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy are warranted.

title: Teleanatomy: A Conceptual Framework for Anatomy Across Distance.
abstract: For centuries, anatomy has been fundamentally grounded in physical proximity. Anatomical knowledge has traditionally been acquired through direct observation of the human body by dissection, surgery, physical examination, and medical imaging. Advances in imaging, three-dimensional modeling, telecommunication, robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and extended reality have transformed how anatomical information is acquired and applied. Although remote anatomical practices already exist in education, imaging, consultation, and surgery, no unified anatomy-specific framework describes how structural information is acquired, represented, transmitted, interpreted, and applied when the anatomical source and the observer or user are spatially separated. We propose teleanatomy as a framework for this distributed setting. Five foundational pillars are identified: acquisition, representation, transmission, interpretation, and application, and three cross-cutting properties, fidelity, provenance, and latency, are proposed as determinants of whether anatomical information remains reliable and fit for purpose. Teleanatomy is not intended to replace digital anatomy, telemedicine, radiologic anatomy, or surgical robotics, but to define the anatomical layer shared by these increasingly remote practices.

title: Time-to-Event Analysis of Clinical Milestones in the ALS Natural History Consortium Dataset.
abstract: Study of clinical milestones, particularly intermediate events like loss of ambulation, in large amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) cohorts is limited. Here, we leverage the ALS Natural History Consortium dataset to evaluate the time-to-event for several outcomes and prognostic factors that predict risk. Longitudinal data from 1950 participants were used in time-to-event analyses based on time from diagnosis. Outcomes were gastrostomy, loss of ambulation, loss of useful speech, non-invasive ventilation (NIV) usage, and death equivalent (death or mechanical ventilation). Median times-to-event were calculated along with Kaplan-Meier curves. Cox proportional hazards models for each outcome estimated (through adjusted hazard ratios [HR]) the impact of several prognostic factors, including sex, region of onset, age at diagnosis, and the initial rate of change (delta-FRS) in ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R) scores. Estimated median times-to-event for clinical outcomes ranged from 1.44 to 6.21 years, with a median time to death equivalent of 2.12 years. A higher delta-FRS was the greatest risk factor for all outcomes (HRs between 2.01 and 3.05). Limb onset decreased risk of loss of speech, NIV use, gastrostomy, and death equivalent (HRs 0.41-0.78). Older age at diagnosis increased risk of gastrostomy, NIV use, and death equivalent (HRs 1.08-1.27). These findings further inform expectations of time to various outcomes, especially rarely investigated intermediate events, and their risk factors. The importance of progression rate supports other recent findings, highlighting delta-FRS as a key prognostic factor with potential utility in clinical trial designs.

title: NEK1 autophosphorylation is disrupted by amyotrophic lateral sclerosis-associated missense variants: activity biomarkers and structural insights.
abstract: Rare variants in NEK1, encoding a serine/threonine kinase, are among the most consistently implicated genetic contributors to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), reported in approximately 2-3% of cases. Yet, while recent studies have characterized the cell biological consequences of NEK1 loss-of-function, the biochemical effects of ALS-associated missense variants on kinase activity have not been directly investigated. This distinction is mechanistically important, because missense alleles encode mutant proteins rather than simply reducing protein dosage. Here, we provide the most comprehensive cell-based phosphoproteomic map of NEK1 phosphorylation to date, identifying 10 recurrent phosphorylation sites across independent expression and acquisition conditions. We experimentally assign pSer14, pThr156 and pSer418 as NEK1 autophosphorylation sites using kinase-dead controls, targeted extracted ion chromatogram analysis, phosphosite mutagenesis and phosphospecific antibodies. Leveraging activation-loop pThr156 as a read-out of NEK1 activity, we assessed nine ALS-associated missense variants spanning the major functional regions of the protein. Among catalytic-domain variants, R261C produced the most robust reduction in pThr156 autophosphorylation, R232C produced a smaller reduction, and R232H increased pThr156; the basic-region variant, A313T, also showed a smaller reduction. Structural modelling provides a mechanistic framework for understanding these variant-specific effects. Our study establishes the first activity-based framework for functional classification of NEK1 missense variants, and provides direct evidence that ALS-associated missense variants can alter NEK1 autophosphorylation through a mechanism distinct from simple haploinsufficiency. The phosphospecific antibodies, isogenic cell lines and curated phosphoproteomic datasets generated here provide a community resource for future studies of NEK1 regulation, variant interpretation and therapeutic target validation.

title: The miR-176-DcFoxO axis links CLas infection to juvenile hormone signaling and enhanced fecundity in Diaphorina citri.
abstract: The phloem-limited bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus (CLas), associated with huanglongbing (HLB) disease, is transmitted by the Asian citrus psyllid, Diaphorina citri. CLas-positive females display enhanced fecundity and increased metabolic demands, a phenotype that may promote both vector population growth and bacterial proliferation.
